headline: MGAT Alpha closed 18 trades this week for a net -$135.14 (22.22% win rate, 4 of 18) -- its weakest week since launch. BC accounted for 11 of the 18 closes and two-thirds of the loss, and the exit mix shifted hard toward stop-losses (13 of 18) as the broader market turned lower. The book still came out ahead of its own hold-and-never-trade benchmark this week -- +4.11% since launch against -4.02% for holding the same seven coins untouched, the first week it has led even stripped of one early outsized print -- but that gap is the basket falling faster than the book, not the book gaining, so the call this week is 'needs improvement'.

counterfactual.reason: The shadow comparison book is void for this run: it could never close a position, so none of its figures measure anything.

hold_benchmark.basis: $8,000 split equally across the seven coins the book bought in its first two cycles on 2026-08-25, held untouched, no fees

llm_adviser: LLM adviser: observer only — logs what it would do, cannot affect a trade (settled from source 2026-09-22).
sample_caveat: 18 closed trades this week, 102 all-time against the 200-trade target (about 51%). All-time is past the floor where win rate and PnL become directional rather than unreadable, but the current losing stretch since the latest restart is only 27 closes, which is under that floor and not yet a meaningful read on its own.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper — simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No CLASS-A changes landed in this week's window, so the comparison with the previous week is clean.

verdict.text: Needs improvement. BC is dragging the book: 11 of 18 closes and -$90.35 of the -$135.14 loss, while the other three families lost smaller amounts on one to five trades each. The exit mix shifted hard toward stop-losses (13 of 18, against roughly a third in the prior stretch), consistent with entries timed into a falling market rather than a broken exit -- the stops fired close to their designed size. Sizing is not the problem: 82% of this week's opens used measured betas, and the measured-beta trades lost money too. Against the hold benchmark the book did better than holding for the first time even with one early outsized print excluded, but that is the basket falling faster than the book, not the book gaining, so it reads as the stop-losses limiting damage rather than an edge. No faults worth separating out this week -- one benign data-source alarm, a clean regime feed, no time-stop overruns. Not yet a 'needs a change' call: losing is an outcome, not automatically a fault, and the current losing stretch is still under the sample floor that would make a structural call safe.
